Dynamic Map and Toshiba study roadside lidar integration with 3D maps

The collaboration will test dynamic road-user data to support autonomous vehicles and mobility inside industrial facilities.

Dynamic Map Platform / PR TIMES ↗27 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Infrastructure data beyond onboard sensors

Selected for Toshiba OPEN INNOVATION PROGRAM 2026, Dynamic Map Platform has begun studying integration of Toshiba Hybrid-3D LiDAR with high-precision 3D maps. The aim is to inform vehicles and fleet systems about people and vehicles that onboard sensors may struggle to see.

Alignment and latency are central

The study covers object types, data formats, interfaces, map alignment, latency, communications and reliability. Lidar point clouds and tracking outputs would be associated with map coordinates before integration into a shared information platform for vehicles and control systems.

Planned demonstrations, not proven outcomes

Proposed settings include intersections, factories, warehouses, ports and airports with mixed traffic, as well as night, rain and fog. The partners plan system definition and demonstrations toward a mid-December 2026 results event. Accident reductions and commercial service availability have not yet been established.
